reviews.text: 🌿 Calm and Beautiful — Beihai Park, Beijing (北海公园) ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5) I recently visited Beihai Park in Beijing, China. Though I couldn’t explore the entire park, the part I did see was truly beautiful. 🌸 🚶‍♂️ Peaceful Walk by the Lake: I walked along the lakeside — the view was calm and refreshing. I was lucky to see a few beautiful mandarins (ducks) swimming in the lake. They looked absolutely gorgeous, and I was mesmerized by their colors and elegance. 🦆✨ 🌳 Nature & Atmosphere: The trees in the park were amazing — tall, green, and perfectly maintained. The entire place felt peaceful, full of fresh air and natural charm. 💭 Impression: Even though I didn’t get the chance to see everything, the little time I spent there was worth it. It’s a great spot to relax, take photos, and enjoy nature in the middle of busy Beijing. 📸 I’ve uploaded some of my favorite photos — hope you enjoy them! ✨ Next Time: I’d love to spend more time exploring the whole park and maybe take a boat ride on the lake. Highly recommended for anyone visiting Beijing! 💡 Travel Tip: Visit Beihai Park in the early morning or late afternoon for the best light and peaceful views by the lake. 🌅

After the majestic, vast, and tourist‑crowded Forbidden City, coming here is an interesting and pleasant experience. When I visited Beijing for the first time (and had no guide), I didn't even think to come here. And that was a pity. The park is located very close to the Forbidden City. Until 1925, it was completely closed off; during the imperial era, it was considered an imperial park. Now it is a lovely place for a walk - you can admire the pond and the stupa (although it is quite far away, and we didn't go there). As many commentators note, there are lots of girls wearing national costumes here. Indeed, there are several spots in Beijing where they gather (you could say they are present at all the major Beijing attractions), but here in the park there are fewer people, so you can see them better -) There are only two costume designs available - representing two different dynasties - that visitors can wear. Of course, an entire industry has sprung up around this, offering costume rentals, makeup services, and professional photo shoots. They look absolutely stunning. If you are visiting the Forbidden City, make sure to stop by Beihai Park to take a break from the crowds, the hustle and bustle, and the city. The park is a perfect place for that.

It is a really beautiful view even though it is expensive. If you want to enter the park, it’s about ¥20 or $3 dollars. It is tricky to navigate without a map and there aren’t any so I recommend that you ask directions to staff. The park is good if you want to go for a little jog or if you want to just look at the statues and learn history.

Beihai Park is one of Beijing’s oldest and most enchanting gardens, with origins that can be traced back as far as the Liao Dynasty. The centerpiece of the park is the vast artificial lake, dug by hand centuries ago, with the soil used to create the hill where the White Dagoba pagoda now stands. This brilliant feat of landscape design reflects the ingenuity of imperial garden planning in ancient China. Walking through the grounds, you get a sense of layered history—emperors once enjoyed these same lake views, shaded corridors, and pavilions. The glistening waters, willow-lined paths, and island temples make it an oasis of calm in the middle of modern Beijing. The White Dagoba on Qionghua Island remains the park’s iconic landmark, visible from many angles and especially beautiful at sunset.

Beihai Park is an absolute gem in the heart of Beijing. The moment you step in, you're transported to a serene world away from the bustling city. The park is vast, with beautiful landscapes that change with the seasons. In summer, the lotus flowers are in full bloom, creating a picturesque scene that's perfect for photos. The island in the middle of the lake is a must-visit, offering a panoramic view of the park and the city beyond. The temples scattered around the park are not only architecturally stunning but also offer a glimpse into the rich history of the place. The White Pagoda, standing tall and majestic, is a sight to behold. It's said to have been built in 1651, and it's a testament to the enduring beauty of ancient Chinese architecture. The park is also home to numerous statues of dragons, each one more intricate than the last. They add a touch of mystique to the already enchanting atmosphere. One of the highlights of my visit was the boat ride. It's a unique way to explore

Pretty park in the middle of Beijing with a big lake. Entry fee is very cheap and can be paid directly at one of the cashiers. Highlight is the white pagoda and the large areas with lotus. Worth a visit to escape the tourist masses around the forbidden city and to enjoy a bit off calm in the middle of the city centre.

It’s a lovely park for a leisurely stroll, with beautiful scenery and a peaceful atmosphere. However, be mindful if you’re visiting on a windy day — the wind tends to be much stronger here due to the open lake and lack of shelter. It can feel quite cold, even in late March. And there would be no boat if it’s windy days…

Beihai Park epitomises the typical elements of Chinese landscape design - careful composition of water bodies, rocks, "mountains", plants, bridges, pavilions. There are also other attractions dotted around the Lake - amongst them is the impressive nine-dragon wall -tucked away in a secluded corner.

The White Dagoba (a stupa) on Jade Flower Island is a moderate hike up a gently sloped hill, and worth the views of the surrounding area as well as the stupa itself. The park's visitors were receptive and welcoming.

There is also a small entrance fee but it was not much. Still worth it if you also wanna take a break from chasing the main attractions of Beijing. Thank you

Beihai Park in Beijing is a stunning oasis amidst the bustling city. Its serene lakes, lush greenery, and historic architecture create a picturesque setting that's truly enchanting. Walking along the winding pathways, you're treated to breathtaking views of ancient pagodas, intricate bridges, and traditional Chinese gardens. The tranquility of the park offers a welcome escape from the urban chaos, allowing visitors to immerse themselves in the beauty of nature and culture. Whether you're strolling by the water's edge, admiring the colorful foliage, or exploring the historical landmarks, Beihai Park captivates with its timeless charm and serene ambiance. It's a must-visit destination for anyone seeking a peaceful retreat in the heart of Beijing.

Beijing Beihai Park is a tranquil oasis nestled in the heart of China's bustling capital. The park's historic significance and scenic beauty make it a must-visit destination. The sprawling grounds are adorned with ancient architecture, including the iconic White Pagoda, offering a glimpse into China's rich cultural heritage. Serene lakes and well-manicured gardens provide a peaceful retreat, inviting visitors to stroll leisurely or take a boat ride. The blend of history, nature, and architecture makes Beihai Park a captivating experience for both locals and tourists alike.

A Journey Through Time at Beihai Park My visit to Beihai Park was like stepping into a living painting. The combination of ancient architecture, lush gardens, and serene waters provided a perfect backdrop for my Chinese costume photoshoot. The park's tranquil atmosphere made it easy to immerse myself in the historical essence of Beijing. Dressed in traditional attire, I felt like I was part of the centuries-old history that surrounds the park. Walking around the iconic White Pagoda and taking in the beautiful views of the lake was both peaceful and inspiring. Each corner of the park offers unique photo opportunities, from the majestic halls to the delicate stone bridges, and I captured some stunning shots in my Chinese costume. Beihai Park is not just a place of beauty; it’s a journey through China’s rich heritage. I highly recommend it to anyone who loves photography, history, and nature, especially if you enjoy dressing in traditional Chinese clothing—this park will elevate your experience to another level!

Beihai Park is a public park and former imperial garden located in the northwestern part of the Imperial City, Beijing. First built in the 11th century, it is among the largest of all Chinese gardens and contains numerous historically important structures, palaces, and temples.

Beihai Park, also known as Northern Sea Park, is a captivating oasis nestled within the heart of Beijing. This expansive imperial garden, with a history spanning over a millennium, offers a serene escape from the bustling city. The park's centerpiece is a vast lake, surrounded by lush gardens, elegant pavilions, and historic structures. One of the highlights is the iconic White Dagoba, a towering white pagoda that stands majestically on an island in the lake. Visitors can rent a boat to get closer to this impressive landmark and enjoy stunning views of the park. The park also houses the Nine Dragon Wall, a magnificent ceramic wall adorned with intricate dragon motifs. Beihai Park is a perfect place to immerse yourself in Chinese history and culture. Whether you're strolling through the tranquil gardens, admiring the ancient architecture, or simply relaxing by the lake, this park offers a peaceful and enriching experience. Here are some additional points to consider when visiting Beihai Park: Timing: The best time to visit is during the spring or autumn when the weather is pleasant. Entrance Fee: There is a small entrance fee to the park. Transportation: The park is easily accessible by public transportation. Food: There are several restaurants and snack stalls within the park. Souvenirs: You can purchase souvenirs at the shops located within the park. Overall, Beihai Park is a must-visit destination for anyone traveling to Beijing. It offers a unique blend of history, culture, and natural beauty, making it a truly unforgettable experience.

Located in the center of Beijing, the Beihai Park is an imperial garden to the northwest of the Forbidden City. It was first built during the Liao Dynasty (907-1125), then continuously rebuilt and renovated in the Jin, Yuan, Ming and Qing dynasties. It is one of the largest Chinese gardens and contains numerous historically important structures, palaces and temples. The Beihai Park covers a total area of 69 hectares, with a lake that occupies more than half of the entire park, and a 32 meters high Qionghua Island. The same as most of Chinese imperial gardens, the Beihai Park was built to imitate the famous scenic spots and architectures from various regions of China: the Taihu Lake, the elaborate pavilions and canals in Hangzhou and Yangzhou, the delicate garden structures in Suzhou and others. The structures and scenes in the Beihai Park are described as masterpieces of gardening technique that reflects the style and the superb architectural skill and richness of traditional Chinese horticulture.

Le parc Beihai se trouve au nord ouest de la Cité Interdite. Facilement accessible par les transports en commun, nous vous conseillons de rentrer par la porte située au nord. L'entrée coûte 10 ¥ par personne. En commençant par le nord, vous pourrez voir toute la grappe des points d'intérêts qui s'y situent, à savoir le mur des neufs dragons, de jolis pavillons, les pavillons des cinq dragons, un jardin chinois traditionnel, etc. Ensuite, revenez sur vos pas pour longer le lac et descendre en direction de l'ile centrale où se trouve un dagoba blanc dont l'accès est payant, soit 20 ¥. Vous trouverez aussi sur cette ile d'autres pavillons, constructions, etc. Même les ponts qui mènent à l'ile méritent le coup d'oeil. C'est un incontournable de Pékin où la vie de tous les jours s'articulent. Vous y verrez de nombreux Chinois venir y faire leur sport, flâner, danser. Prévoir 2h car le parc est grand.

愛新覺羅溥儀的私家財產 去過故宮的都會很吃驚，蝦米，御花園竟然這麼小，但只要再往後走，就有個超大的北海公園，皇家氣勢終究是有地。 於民國年間，還是愛新覺羅溥儀的私家財產，1979年後對公眾開放，如果行程裏真的排不進去頤和園，那在北海公園也能過過乾癮，景致相當秀氣漂亮。 跟我五年前去相比，北海公園新開了一些景點 建議可以好好逛一圈，每一個景點都很有漂亮 拍起來特別有味道 我最初是為了九龍壁去的，後來還把其它三塊也搜集好了 關於九龍壁： 中國現存九龍壁有四處，北海公園的位在北海北岸王殿西，是一座彩色琉璃磚影壁，影壁用424塊彩色琉璃瓦砌成，壁面有九條形態各異的蟠龍，奔騰於波濤雲際之中，是清代琉璃建築中的傑作。 其它三塊分別在大同、山西、故宮 ˙大同九龍壁，位於大同市城區，是最大，歷史最悠久的一個。原為明太祖朱元璋第十三代孫朱桂的王府前的照壁。 ˙山西平遙九龍壁，在平遙古城的平遙文廟內，建於明朝初期，原為太子寺照壁。文化大革命中被破壞，後修復。 ˙故宮九龍壁，位於北京市故宮內，寧壽門前的影壁，建於乾隆三十八年（1773年）。

北海公園位於北京西城區、故宮西北處，是中國保存最完整、最悠久、最具代表性的皇家園林之一，始建於遼代，至今已有上千年的歷史；北海公園占地69公頃，其中水面占39公頃，是中國歷史園林的藝術傑作，北海主要由瓊島景區、東岸景區、北岸景區、團城景區、北海植物園等五個部分組成；目前北海公園內經常舉辦書法展、花卉展，種植許多深具特色的園林植物，是中國園林藝術的瑰寶，還提供各式特色船隻，讓您能乘著古色古香的船遊北海。 由於明朝永樂18年將首都遷至北京，因此北海公園中太液池、萬壽山成為紫禁城西面的御苑，統稱西苑，接著向南開拓水面，形成北海、南海及中海，三海格局，成為為皇城內最重要的皇家園林；北海公園的太液池水面廣闊，面積39公頃，其南部的瓊島是北海公園的主體，島上建築精美，景色幽靜，別具一格，東邊有陟山橋連岸，南邊有永安橋與團城緊連。 團城位於北海公園南門外西側，是座用磚築成的圓形別緻小城，高4.6公尺，面積4553平方公尺。團城的主體建築物－承光殿位於中央，其平面呈帶折角的十字形，殿前後為方形月臺，中央為重簷大殿，殿堂華麗、飛簷翹角、宏麗軒昂，至清代改為佛堂，內供白玉佛。 白塔聳立瓊島之巔，建於1651年，高35.9公尺，直徑14公尺，上層為覆缽式塔身，下層塔座為折角式須彌座，門內刻有藏文咒語，正面有壺門式眼光門，成為北海公園的象徵；白塔前有一善因殿，上圓下方，殿外四壁鑲有455尊佛像；白塔山西坡有一座閱古樓，平面近似橢圓形的兩層樓宇，樓內壁間嵌滿《三希堂法帖》等石刻以及自魏晉以來歷代墨蹟，是中國古代書法藝術中的精華；白塔山東坡有一座乾隆瓊島春蔭石碑，立於綠蔭深處，為燕京八景之一。 北海公園內的九龍壁位在北海北岸天王殿西，建於乾隆21年(1756年)，長27公尺、壁高5公尺，是一座彩色琉璃磚影壁，影壁用424塊彩色琉璃瓦砌成，壁面有九條形態各異的蟠龍，奔騰於波濤雲際之中，有詩云：『九龍盤拿戲驪珠，雲霧冥冥蜃氣孤，恍惚電光來破壁，半空飛出所翁圖』，是清代琉璃建築中的傑作

Es una gran aventura. Mucha historia la que posee este recinto. El Parque Beihai fue construido como un jardín imperial durante la dinastía, entre los años 1115-1234. En 1961 fue declarado Sitio de Protección de Reliquias Culturales Nacionales. Este lugar es consideradi uno de los mayores jardines chinos, y contiene muchas estructuras, palacios y templos de importancia histórica. Entre las insfraestructura destacan: ♕ La Pagoda Blanca es una edificación budista de 40 m de altura, situada en el punto más alto de la Isla Qiónghuá. ♕Falin Dian. El salón más importante del templo de Yong an, alberga las imágenes del Buda. #BeihaiPark #china #beijingtrip #instaphoto

El mejor momento es al atardecer; cenar y tomar algo en este lugar es genial. La foto que muestro es la Pagoda Blanca 白塔, que fue construida por motivo del Dalai Lama quién visitó Beijing en 1651. Por esta razón se construyó esta enorme "tulipa" blanca levantada sobre la isla central del lago. Está situada al norte de la Ciudad Prohibida; cerca también de la Colina del Carbón.

ここは現存する皇室庭園の中で世界最古と言われています。北京にある三つの大きな湖「西苑三海」の一つ、北海の周辺に広がる広大な御苑跡です。日々進化する北京の真ん中にありながら、ここだけはまるで時間が止まっているかのような静けさに包まれていました。 公園の歴史はおよそ1000年前の遼代にまで遡ると言います。その後、王朝が幾度となく変わっても、この北海は歴代の皇帝たちの庭であり続けました。元朝のフビライ・ハンは、ここを中心に現在の北京の前身である大都を造営したとされ、「先に北海あり、後に北京あり」という言葉があるほど、北京の歴史に深く関わっています。 湖が織りなす壮大な造園様式 公園の総面積は約70万平方メートルで、その半分以上を湖が占めています。これは皇室庭園にのみ許された「一池三山」という造園様式で、東の海に不老不死の仙人が住むという伝説の三神山（蓬莱、瀛州、方丈）を、園内の瓊華島、団城、犀山台に見立てているそうです。 園内はとても広く、すべてを見て回るにはかなりの時間が必要です。私も、紫禁城観光の後に訪れたため、九龍壁などの有名な建物や、白塔のある島を巡るだけでも十分な散策になりました。 美しい景色と市民の憩い この公園は、湖に映る楼閣や豊かな自然の情景が、ことのほか美しいと感じました。湖ではボートを借りて楽しむこともでき、風の強い日には運航していませんでしたが、静かな湖面をゆっくりと進むのも素敵でしょう。 入場料はとても手頃で、窓口でチケットをすぐに購入できます。紫禁城のような混雑はなく、地元の人々が太極拳やダンスを楽しんでいて、静かで穏やかな雰囲気に包まれています。 ただ、週末や休日は混雑することもあると聞いています。もし静かな時間を過ごしたいなら、平日の訪問が良いかもしれません。

Công viên Bắc Hải nằm trên một hòn đảo nhỏ ở trung tâm thủ đô Bắc Kinh, phía tây bắc Tử Cấm Thành. Đây là một trong những khu vườn hoàng gia lâu đời nhất tại Trung Quốc, thường được ví von là “viên ngọc xanh giữa lòng thành phố”. Công viên được xây dựng cách đây hàng nghìn năm, trải qua các triều đại Nguyên, Minh và Thanh. - Khu vườn cổ rộng đến 71 ha, trong đó có 39 ha là diện tích mặt nước, tiêu biểu cho nghệ thuật vườn tinh tế và hoàn hảo của Trung Hoa. Với không gian yên bình cùng cảnh quan tuyệt đẹp, Bắc Hải là điểm đến yêu thích của các vị vua chúa và tầng lớp quý tộc xưa. Đến thăm thủ đô Bắc Kinh, du khách nhất định phải dành thời gian ghé qua khu vườn cổ này. - Du khách có thể đến tham quan công viên Bắc Hải vào bất kỳ thời điểm nào trong năm. Tuy nhiên, để có được những bức ảnh đẹp thì bạn hãy chọn những ngày trời nắng ráo. Theo kinh nghiệm của các tín đồ du lịch, thời điểm lý tưởng nhất để du ngoạn Bắc Kinh là từ tháng 3 - tháng 11. Nếu muốn tham dự Lễ hội hoa sen, du khách nên đi vào khoảng thời gian từ tháng 7 – tháng 8. - Từ Việt Nam, du khách có thể đến Bắc Kinh thăm công viên Bắc Hải bằng các chuyến bay xuất phát từ Hà Nội, TP.HCM và Đà Nẵng. Thời gian bay trung bình đối với các chuyến bay thẳng là 3 tiếng, chuyến bay có quá cảnh sẽ mất nhiều thời gian hơn. Truy cập Traveloka để tìm kiếm giá tốt, chọn hạng vé và thanh toán ngay trên ứng dụng. - Từ trung tâm Bắc Kinh, bạn có thể đến công viên bằng tàu điện ngầm hoặc xe buýt. Nếu đi tàu điện ngầm, bạn hãy chọn Line 6, xuống ở ga Beihai Bei. Từ cổng B của ga tàu, bạn đi bộ về phía đông thêm tầm 5 phút là đến được cổng bắc của công viên. - Lịch sử của công viên Bắc Hải bắt nguồn từ một câu chuyện truyền thuyết cổ xưa trong văn hoá Trung Hoa. Vào thời Chiến Quốc, tức thế kỷ thứ III TCN, ở phía đông hồ Bắc Hải có 3 ngọn núi thần là Ưng Châu, Bồng Lai và Trương Phương. Các vị tiên ngự trên núi đã tu luyện thành công một phương thuốc trường sinh bất lão. Tin đồn về thuốc trường sinh nhanh chóng lan truyền khắp đất nước, các vị vua qua các triều đại không ngừng tìm kiếm phương thuốc kỳ diệu này. - Năm 221 TCN, Tần Thuỷ Hoàng đã cho nhà giả kim Từ Phúc cùng tuỳ tùng đi tìm 3 ngọn núi thần này nhưng không thành công. Tần Thuỷ Hoàng sau đó đã cho xây dựng một hồ nước lớn ngay trong hoàng cung, đắp đất tạo ra 3 ngọn núi giả. Trải qua nhiều triều đại, khu vườn tiếp tục được tu bổ và đổi mới. Quy mô hiện tại của công viên có công lớn của hoàng đế Càn Long – người đã cho xây dựng lại và mở rộng diện tích. Không chỉ mở rộng công viên Bắc Hải, vua Càn Long còn cho cải tạo nơi đây thành một khu vườn hoàng gia. Các công trình kiến trúc được xây dựng cực kỳ hoành tráng, từ đền đài, vườn cây cho đến hồ nước. Nơi đây là địa điểm nghỉ ngơi, thư giãn của vua chúa và giới quý tộc, đồng thời cũng là trung tâm văn hoá – nghệ thuật thu hút các học giả, nghệ sĩ. - Công viên chính thức mở cửa cho công chúng vào tham quan từ năm 1925 và nhanh chóng trở thành điểm tham quan hấp dẫn tại Bắc Kinh. Các tòa cung điện tráng lệ kết hợp cùng các công trình kiến trúc tôn giáo trang nghiêm đã tạo nên một chỉnh thể hoàn mỹ đến từng chi tiết. Taman Behai, Beijing Beihai Park merupakan obyek wisata berupa taman kerajaan. Beihai Park menjadi salah satu taman tertua di Beijing yang terletak di sebelah utara Forbidden City. Taman seluas lebih dari 69 hektar ini dibangun pada sekitar abad ke-10 dan dibuka untuk umum pada tahun 1925. Sejak dibuka untuk umum saat pertama kali hingga sekarang, Beihai Park menjadi salah satu obyek wisata favorit bagi siapa saja yang berkunjung ke kota Beijing. Lebih dari separuh taman ini merupakan danau. Tepat berada di danau di tengah taman ini terdapat sebuah pulau yang bernama Qionghua Island. Di pulau ini pula terdapat sebuah pagoda berwana putih yang dibangun oleh kaisar untuk menghormati para leluhur. Pagoda setinggi 32 meter ini merupakan salah satu daya tarik dari Beihai Park karena memiliki desain dan ornament yang unik.

北海公園位於中華人民共和國北京市城區的中偏北部，故宮和景山的西北側，始建於遼代，是世界上現存建園時間最早的皇家宮苑。北海的布局以瓊華島為主體，在島的頂端建有標誌性建築永安寺白塔，與南岸的團城、北岸的宮苑群遙相呼應，相互借景，構成園林的南北中軸線。 北海先後歷經遼、金、元、明、清五朝的興建，歷史悠久且重建時承襲較多。它始建於遼代，當時位於遼南京城的東北郊外，附近風景秀麗，於是統治者便疏浚水系，仿照蓬萊仙境建造了瑤嶼行宮。金大定十九年（1179年）起，在瑤嶼行宮的基礎上疊石造山，修建了廣寒殿，同時將湖泊稱為「西華潭」，瑤嶼改名為「瓊華島」，將整座離宮命名為「大寧宮」（後來又改稱「萬寧宮」）。 元代以瓊華島為中心規劃了大都城，在中統三年（1262年）、至元四年（1267年）和至正八年（1348年）三次擴建瓊華島，將山命名為「萬壽山」（或「萬歲山」），湖命名為「太液池」。同時還在太液池的東岸修建了大內皇宮，在西岸建造了隆福宮和興聖宮，構成一座巨大的宮苑——「上苑」。 明代永樂十八年（1420年），明王朝定都北京後，在太液池以東建造了皇宮紫禁城，並向南拓展水系，形成中海、南海，與北海一起合稱「西苑」，劃入皇城的範圍。萬曆七年（1579年），廣寒殿倒塌，此後一直沒有修復，直到清代順治八年（1651年），才應喇嘛所請，在廣寒殿舊址上興建了白塔，並將島南部的宮殿改建為永安寺。清代乾隆六年（1741年）起，北海開始了長達三十年的擴建，除了在瓊華島的四面廣建庭軒樓榭外，還在太液池的北岸和東岸增加了許多建築群，形成今日的格局。 清代末光緒十一年（1885年），慈禧太后私自動用海軍軍費增修過北海。1900年八國聯軍攻占北京時，對北海有過較大的破壞，兩年後進行了重建。 中華民國時期，按《清皇室優待條例》，北海先是成為愛新覺羅溥儀的私家財產，後來1925年愛新覺羅皇室遷離紫禁城悉後，起闢作公園，但一直沒有對公眾開放。 中華人民共和國成立後，中南海成為了中央人民政府的駐地，北海作為公園開放。1961年，北海及團城被中華人民共和國國務院公布為第一批全國重點文物保護單位之一。1969年至1979年，北海公園以「保護中南海安全」為由關閉，禁止遊人入內。1979年後北海公園重新對公眾開放。1996年，北海被列入聯合國教育科學文化組織世界文化遺產後備名錄 北海全園占地約70公頃，其中水域占據了一半以上的面積。太池中有瓊華、團城和犀山台三島，分別象徵著蓬萊、瀛洲和方丈，體現了對蓬萊仙境的追求。是一座純粹的人工園林，布局以水為主體，在太液池中布置島嶼，用橋和岸邊相連。太液池的池水原經金水河直接引自玉泉山，明代起取自積水潭。池中有瓊華、團城和犀山台三島，分別象徵著蓬萊、瀛洲和方丈，體現了對蓬萊意境的追求。它的建築風格受到一些江南園林的影響，但總體上仍然保持了北方園林持重端莊的特點。園內宗教色彩十分濃厚，不僅瓊華島上有永安寺，在北岸和東岸還有闡福寺、西天梵境、小西天、龍王廟、先蠶壇等佛教、道教建築，因此是一座集宮室、宅第、寺廟、園林於一體的宏大帝王宮苑。 瓊華島位於北海的中偏南部，太液池中，是整座園林的核心。金代稱瓊華島，元代曾一度改名為萬壽山。「燕京八景」之一的「瓊島春蔭」指的就是湖心的瓊華島。瓊化島上的白塔也成為北海形象的代表。著名兒童歌曲《讓我們盪起雙槳》中的歌詞「讓我們盪起雙槳，小船兒推開波浪，水面倒映著美麗的白塔，四周環繞著綠樹紅牆」描繪的正是泛舟太液池的景致。島上建築均依山而建，高低錯落有致，大體可分為東南西北四個部分。 瓊華島的西坡山腰有琳光殿、甘露殿、水精域、蟠青室等組成的建築群。其北側的閱古樓是座皇家藏書樓，平面呈半月形，共有兩層，上下共25間，左右合抱，內有螺旋樓梯。在樓內牆壁上鑲嵌了《三希堂法帖》刻石495方，囊括魏晉以來134位書法家的墨跡精華，其中王羲之《快雪時晴帖》、王獻之《中秋帖》、王珣《伯遠帖》等三件墨寶都堪稱稀世奇珍，被乾隆帝譽為「三稀」。 山的北坡分為山麓和臨水兩部分。山麓建築有抱沖室、一壺天地、酣古堂、盤嵐精舍、得勝樓等。在山坡下，是臨水而建的漪瀾堂、道寧齋、碧照樓、遠帆閣等一組亭台樓榭，風格參照了鎮江的金山寺。其兩側有長300米的半圓形雙層長廊，東西分別連接倚晴樓和分水閣，與太液池北岸的五龍亭、西天梵境等建築隔水相望，交相輝映。在西北側的山坡上還有乾隆時建造的仙人承露盤，是雕刻在蟠龍石柱上的一尊以雙手承托露盤的仙人像，總高5.5米。 山的東坡建築不多，有智珠殿、半月城和見春亭等。這一片林木成蔭，怪石嶙峋，崖洞深邃，景色幽靜。「燕京八景」之一的「瓊島春蔭」就是指此，至今林蔭內還保留著一塊乾隆帝題詩的「瓊島春蔭」幢形碑。

El Parque Beihai es uno de los parques más importantes de Beijing. Por su emplazamiento, cercano a la Ciudad Prohibida y a los Lagos Houhai, la visita al parque puede combinarse fácilmente. Durante los fines de semana se convierte en un refugio que atrae a miles de visitantes, pekineses y foráneos, por lo que se recomienda ir entre semana si se busca el alejarse de la vida caótica de Beijing por un rato. La entrada es muy económica y se pueden comprar dos tipos de tickets: para pasear por el parque únicamente o combinado con el acceso a los puntos de interés (zona de la isla Qiong, con la Pagoda Blanca como punto más alto). Además, existen embarcaciones de recreo para disfrutar del lago. Hay también baños públicos y diversos locales de bebidas y comidas (sin pretensiones). Para los turistas, una visita completa y no estresada rondaría las 3-4 horas.
